orientation.top_of_map: west wall (the wall with the low curtain and the little door); the hall's north end is at the left edge, the south end at the right edge
orientation.note_en: camera positions in views[] are described relative to these landmarks; xy_m = xy x map_extent_m (origin top-left). As drawn, the hall floor spans about x 0.11-0.90, y 0.35-0.64; everything outside the wall lines is solid masonry. SCN-pool-of-tears has its own frame and coordinates (its image is framed differently).

views.desc_en: eye-level wide establishing shot from just inside the corner entrance down the long low hall, the row of hanging lamps leading to the small glass table far down the centre line, locked doors on both walls
eye-level medium shot from beside the glass table across to the low crimson curtain at the base of the west wall, between two locked horseshoe-arched doors
low close shot from the floor at the curtain back toward the glass table, its three clear legs and the golden key glinting on the top far above
high oblique wide shot from above the far south door looking back the whole length of the hall to the dark corner entrance, the lamp pools stepping away along the flag floor
eye-level medium shot from the centre of the hall under the lamps toward the locked oak doors of the west wall, their iron locks and the stained-glass roundels above them
eye-level close shot toward one locked door of the east wall: the large black iron lock and keyhole, the whiplash iron frame and mosaic dado
eye-level medium shot from the glass table on down the hall toward the far south door and the last lamps
high oblique wide shot from above the south-east doors diagonally back up the hall toward the blind north end wall, the full rhythm of doors and vault ribs visible
eye-level close shot straight across the hall from the south-east doors to the low curtain on the opposite wall, hinting at the little door hidden behind it

calibration.method: landmark xy re-measured on the delivered layout_top.png (door/opening landmarks read at the gap in the wall line)
